lessonTitle: The Bilaminar Disc and Gastrulation: Epiblast, Hypoblast, Primitive Streak and Notochord

blocks.text: A home pregnancy test detects a hormone made by cells that have invaded the uterine wall only a week or so after fertilisation, long before the embryo is bigger than a pinhead. Those same days build a two-layered disc from which every tissue of the body will be generated. What happens in weeks 2 and 3?

blocks.markdown: **Counting the days.** In embryology, age is usually counted from fertilisation (day 0), whereas in clinical obstetrics gestational age is counted from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP). In a regular 28-day cycle ovulation and fertilisation occur about 14 days after the LMP, so gestational age is about 2 weeks more than embryonic age. This lesson uses embryonic (post-fertilisation) days. Implantation begins around day 6-7, and by the end of week 2 the embryo is a **bilaminar** (two-layer) disc; in week 3 it becomes a **trilaminar** (three-layer) disc by the process of gastrulation.

blocks.title: Epiblast and hypoblast
blocks.text: At about day 8 the inner cell mass of the blastocyst differentiates into two layers. The epiblast is a layer of tall columnar cells facing the amniotic cavity; the hypoblast is a layer of small cuboidal cells facing the blastocyst cavity (future yolk sac). Together they form the bilaminar embryonic disc. All three germ layers of the embryo will come from the epiblast.

blocks.markdown: **Week 2 events.** (1) A fluid-filled **amniotic cavity** opens within the epiblast; its roof is formed by amnioblasts. (2) The trophoblast differentiates into an inner **cytotrophoblast** (mononucleated, proliferating) and an outer **syncytiotrophoblast** (multinucleated, invasive). The syncytiotrophoblast erodes maternal endometrial vessels and secretes **human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)**, which maintains the corpus luteum and is the basis of pregnancy tests. (3) Hypoblast cells spread to line the blastocyst cavity, forming the primary (exocoelomic) yolk sac. (4) Loose **extraembryonic mesoderm** fills the space between the cytotrophoblast and the yolk sac; it then splits and forms the **chorionic cavity**. The extraembryonic mesoderm that remains suspending the embryo in this cavity is the **connecting stalk**, the future umbilical cord attachment. By the end of week 2 the disc is suspended in the chorionic cavity between the amniotic cavity and the (now secondary) yolk sac.

blocks.title: Dating the events of week 2
blocks.prompt: A woman with regular 28-day cycles has an LMP on 1 March. Fertilisation occurs on 15 March (day 0). Place the following events on the calendar: blastocyst starts to implant (day 6), bilaminar disc present (day 8), end of week 2 (day 14). Is the pregnancy test likely to be positive on her expected period date?

steps.text: Fertilisation is day 0 = 15 March. Implantation begins on day 6 = 21 March.
The bilaminar disc with epiblast and hypoblast is present by day 8 = 23 March, and the syncytiotrophoblast has already begun secreting hCG.
End of week 2 is day 14 = 29 March. Her expected period would be due 29 March (28-day cycle from 1 March), which is also embryonic day 14.
hCG has been produced since implantation, so a sensitive urine test is likely to be positive around the time of the missed period.

blocks.answer: Implantation starts about 21 March, the bilaminar disc is formed by about 23 March, and by the expected period date (29 March, embryonic day 14) hCG is detectable, so the test is likely to be positive.

blocks.markdown: **Gastrulation (week 3).** About day 15 a thickening, the **primitive streak**, appears in the midline on the dorsal surface of the epiblast at the caudal end of the disc. Its cranial end forms a raised **primitive node** (with a **primitive pit**). The streak defines the *craniocaudal axis* and the *left-right* sides of the embryo. Epiblast cells move toward the streak, undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and **invaginate** through it. Signalling molecules such as Nodal and fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) drive this migration. The cells that enter first displace the hypoblast and form **definitive (embryonic) endoderm**; cells that enter next spread between epiblast and endoderm as **intraembryonic mesoderm**; the cells that stay on the surface become **ectoderm**. Thus the epiblast gives rise to all three germ layers, and the hypoblast contributes no cells to the embryo proper (it is replaced by endoderm).

rows: Epiblast cells that do not ingress through the streak
Epiblast cells that migrate through the streak and spread laterally between the other layers
First wave of ingressing epiblast cells that replace the hypoblast
blocks.caption: The three germ layers established by gastrulation.

blocks.markdown: **Notochord.** Cells that enter at the primitive pit migrate in the midline cranially as a tube, the **notochordal process**, which then fuses into a solid rod, the **notochord**. It lies between ectoderm and endoderm, in the midline, from the cranial end of the node toward the prechordal plate. The notochord is the first midline axis of the embryo and has three main roles: it **induces the overlying ectoderm** to thicken into the **neural plate** (the start of the nervous system); it signals to surrounding mesoderm to form the vertebral column; and its remnants persist as the **nucleus pulposus** of each intervertebral disc. At the extreme cranial and caudal ends of the disc ectoderm and endoderm remain fused with no mesoderm between them, forming the **oropharyngeal (buccopharyngeal) membrane** and the **cloacal membrane**, future openings of the gut.

blocks.title: Induction
blocks.text: Induction is the process by which one group of cells (the inducer) signals to another group and changes its fate. The notochord inducing the neural plate in the overlying ectoderm is the textbook example; the primitive streak also acts as an organiser of the body axes.

blocks.title: Where does a cell end up, based on when it enters the streak?
blocks.prompt: Epiblast cell X invaginates through the primitive streak in the first wave and moves into the hypoblast layer; cell Y enters later and spreads laterally between the layers; cell Z never enters the streak. State the fate of each, and what would happen to the neural plate if the cells of the notochordal process failed to form.

steps.text: Cell X enters first and displaces the hypoblast, so it becomes definitive endoderm.
Cell Y enters later and lies between the epiblast and the endoderm, so it becomes intraembryonic mesoderm.
Cell Z remains in the epiblast layer facing the amniotic cavity, so it becomes ectoderm.
The notochord induces the neural plate in the overlying ectoderm, so without a notochord the midline ectoderm would receive no inductive signal and neural plate formation would be deficient.

blocks.answer: X becomes endoderm, Y mesoderm and Z ectoderm; absent notochord means failed or abnormal neural plate induction.

items: Day 8: epiblast and hypoblast form the bilaminar disc; amniotic cavity appears in the epiblast.
Days 8-12: syncytiotrophoblast invades and secretes hCG; primary yolk sac forms from the hypoblast.
Days 12-14: extraembryonic mesoderm, chorionic cavity and connecting stalk form; secondary yolk sac.
Day 15: primitive streak and node appear on the dorsal epiblast.
Days 15-17: epiblast cells ingress, forming endoderm then mesoderm; ectoderm remains; notochord forms.

blocks.title: Remnants of the primitive streak
blocks.text: The streak normally regresses and disappears by the end of week 4. Persistent streak remnants in the sacrococcygeal region can give rise to a sacrococcygeal teratoma, a tumour containing tissues from all three germ layers, because the streak cells are pluripotent. This is a clinical reminder that the streak is the source of all germ layers.

points: In week 2 the inner cell mass becomes the bilaminar disc: epiblast (facing the amniotic cavity) and hypoblast (facing the yolk sac); the syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG.
Gastrulation in week 3 begins with the primitive streak: epiblast cells ingress to make endoderm, then mesoderm, leaving the remainder as ectoderm.
The notochord forms from cells migrating from the primitive node; it induces the neural plate and later persists as the nucleus pulposus.
The oropharyngeal and cloacal membranes are sites where ectoderm and endoderm remain in contact without mesoderm.

questions.stem: Which cell layer secretes human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) during implantation?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the multinucleated outer trophoblast secretes hCG.
distractorRationale.b: The hypoblast forms the yolk sac lining and does not secrete hCG.
distractorRationale.c: The epiblast gives rise to the embryo and amnion, not hCG.
distractorRationale.d: The cytotrophoblast is the proliferative stem layer; the hormone-secreting layer is the syncytiotrophoblast.

questions.explanation: The cytotrophoblast divides and its cells fuse to form the outer syncytiotrophoblast, which invades the endometrium and secretes hCG. hCG maintains the corpus luteum and is the basis of pregnancy tests.

questions.stem: The bilaminar embryonic disc consists of which two layers?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the epiblast (dorsal) and hypoblast (ventral) make up the bilaminar disc.
distractorRationale.b: These are the two layers of the trophoblast, which is extraembryonic.
distractorRationale.c: These are germ layers formed after gastrulation, in the trilaminar disc (with mesoderm).
distractorRationale.d: The amnion and chorion are extraembryonic membranes.

questions.explanation: The inner cell mass splits into the epiblast and hypoblast at about day 8. The trophoblast layers are extraembryonic, and ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm do not exist until gastrulation in week 3.

questions.stem: During gastrulation, which of the following correctly describes the fate of the hypoblast?

options.text: It is displaced by epiblast-derived cells that form definitive endoderm
It gives rise to the notochord

questions.correctOptionText: It is displaced by epiblast-derived cells that form definitive endoderm

distractorRationale.a: Correct: epiblast cells passing through the streak replace the hypoblast as definitive endoderm.
distractorRationale.b: Mesoderm arises from epiblast cells passing through the streak, not from the hypoblast.
distractorRationale.c: The neural plate is thickened ectoderm, derived from epiblast.
distractorRationale.d: The notochord arises from epiblast cells that migrate from the primitive node.

questions.explanation: All three germ layers derive from the epiblast. The first ingressing epiblast cells displace the hypoblast and become definitive endoderm, so the hypoblast contributes to extraembryonic structures such as the yolk sac lining rather than to the embryo proper.

questions.stem: In an experiment on a model embryo, cells of the notochord are selectively destroyed at the equivalent of day 18. Which immediate developmental effect is most expected?

options.text: The overlying ectoderm fails to be induced to form a neural plate
The embryo does not form an amniotic cavity
The syncytiotrophoblast fails to secrete hCG
The connecting stalk is not formed

questions.correctOptionText: The overlying ectoderm fails to be induced to form a neural plate

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the notochord is the inducer of the neural plate.
distractorRationale.b: The amniotic cavity forms in week 2, before the notochord exists.
distractorRationale.c: hCG secretion by the syncytiotrophoblast is an extraembryonic event, independent of the notochord.
distractorRationale.d: The connecting stalk forms from extraembryonic mesoderm in week 2.

questions.explanation: The notochord lies beneath the midline ectoderm and induces it to thicken into the neural plate. Events of week 2 (amniotic cavity, hCG secretion and the connecting stalk) occur before the notochord exists and do not depend on it.

questions.stem: Where are ectoderm and endoderm in direct contact without intervening mesoderm in the trilaminar disc?

options.text: At the oropharyngeal membrane and the cloacal membrane
Along the entire length of the notochord
Throughout the lateral edges of the disc

questions.correctOptionText: At the oropharyngeal membrane and the cloacal membrane

distractorRationale.a: Correct: these are the two places where ectoderm and endoderm are fused without mesoderm.
distractorRationale.b: The notochord is a mesodermal structure lying between the two layers.
distractorRationale.c: The primitive node is where cells ingress into the middle layer.
distractorRationale.d: Mesoderm spreads laterally throughout the disc except cranially and caudally at these membranes.

questions.explanation: Intraembryonic mesoderm spreads between ectoderm and endoderm everywhere except at the cranial oropharyngeal membrane and the caudal cloacal membrane. These membranes later rupture to open the mouth and the anus/urogenital opening.

questions.stem: A woman with regular 28-day cycles has a last menstrual period that began 31 days ago and fertilisation occurred at the usual time in her cycle (14 days after the LMP). What is the embryonic age, counted from fertilisation, in days?
questions.explanation: Embryonic age equals gestational age minus the roughly 14 days between the LMP and fertilisation in a 28-day cycle: 31 - 14 = 17 days. At day 17 the embryo is in the third week, during gastrulation, when epiblast cells are ingressing through the primitive streak.

questions.stem: True or false: The primitive streak forms on the ventral surface of the hypoblast at the cranial end of the disc.
questions.explanation: The primitive streak forms in the dorsal epiblast at the caudal end of the disc, with the node at its cranial end. The hypoblast is the ventral layer and does not give rise to the streak.

questions.stem: Describe how gastrulation converts the bilaminar disc into a trilaminar disc, naming the structure through which cells move, the order in which layers form, and the origin of each layer.
markingGuide: Primitive streak appears on the dorsal surface of the epiblast at the caudal end around day 15, with a node at the cranial end.
Epiblast cells migrate to the streak and ingress (invaginate) through it, undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
The first ingressing cells displace the hypoblast and form definitive endoderm.
Later cells spread between epiblast and endoderm as intraembryonic mesoderm.
Epiblast cells that remain on the surface become ectoderm.
All three layers therefore derive from the epiblast.
questions.explanation: Gastrulation is epiblast ingression through the primitive streak. The first wave replaces the hypoblast as endoderm, the next becomes mesoderm and what remains is ectoderm, so all layers are epiblast derived.

questions.stem: Describe the formation of the notochord and state three of its roles in development.
markingGuide: Cells ingress at the primitive pit/node and migrate cranially in the midline as the notochordal process.
The process fuses into a solid rod, the notochord, between ectoderm and endoderm.
It induces the overlying ectoderm to form the neural plate.
It signals to mesoderm to form the vertebral column (axial skeleton) and defines the midline axis.
Its remnants persist as the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral discs.
questions.explanation: The notochord arises from the primitive node as a midline rod and is the first axial structure. It acts as an inducer of the neural plate and the vertebral column, and persists as nucleus pulposus.

questions.stem: Describe the changes that convert the blastocyst's inner cell mass into the bilaminar disc in week 2, and state two functions of the syncytiotrophoblast.
markingGuide: Inner cell mass differentiates into epiblast (columnar, adjacent to amniotic cavity) and hypoblast (cuboidal, adjacent to blastocyst cavity).
An amniotic cavity forms within the epiblast.
Hypoblast cells line the blastocyst cavity to form the primary yolk sac.
Syncytiotrophoblast invades the endometrium and erodes maternal vessels, aiding implantation and nutrient exchange.
Syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG, maintaining the corpus luteum.
questions.explanation: By day 8 the embryonic cells are in two layers with an amniotic cavity above and yolk sac below. The syncytiotrophoblast invades the endometrium and secretes hCG.
